literal_meaning: The analogy of ants eating up the jaggery store.
explanation: The sweet store is something the ants will keep returning to. The dictionary applies the image to work that must always be guarded carefully against an enemy. Its emphasis is continuing exposure, rather than a single finished loss. Unlike putting an ant in charge of the store, this analogy does not appoint the eater as guardian.
meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ଘରକୁ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆସିବା ଥରେ ଜଗିଦେଲେ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯିବା ପରି ନୁହେଁ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ ସର୍ବଦା ସାବଧାନତା ସହ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାକୁ ଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ଜୋର ଲଗାତାର ସତର୍କତା ଉପରେ। ଗୁଡ଼ଘରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିକୁ ଜଗୁଆଳି କରିବାର ଅନ୍ୟ ନ୍ୟାୟଠାରୁ ଏହା ଅଲଗା; ଏଠାରେ ଖାଦକକୁ ରକ୍ଷାର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଦେବା କଥା ନାହିଁ।
english_summary: The source applies the sweet-store image to work needing continuing protection.
odia_summary: ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ସାବଧାନରେ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର।

title: Ants eating through the jaggery store
usage_example: A club restores its noticeboard after repeated deliberate damage. When someone says one repair has settled the matter, another member uses the jaggery-store analogy to explain why they still need to watch it. (Original imagined use.)
cultural_context: The source says enemy, not merely accident or ordinary wear. The new example therefore retains deliberate interference. Note1 in this same source is the different guardian/conflict-of-interest analogy; keep the two separate.
